title: Ergodic topology sampling toward the continuum with Stochastic Normalizing Flows
authors: Claudio Bonanno, Andrea Bulgarelli, Elia Cellini, Alessandro Nada, Dario Panfalone, Davide Vadacchino, Lorenzo Verzichelli
abstract: In this work we provide numerical evidence that topological freezing in $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ Yang-Mills theory can be mitigated with a flow-based approach, as tested at lattice spacings as fine as 0.03~fm. We do so by analyzing the scaling of the costs of a computational strategy based on the combination of open boundary conditions and Stochastic Normalizing Flows. We show that the integrated autocorrelation time of the squared topological charge and the statistical uncertainty on the topological susceptibility remain under control throughout the explored parameter range with currently available computational resources. This marks an important step toward the use of even more efficient flow-based architectures for ergodic sampling of topology in state-of-the-art lattice gauge theory calculations.
summary: This work introduces a novel computational strategy combining Stochastic Normalizing Flows (SNFs) with open-to-periodic boundary condition evolution to overcome topological freezing in SU(3) Yang-Mills theory. By controlling the autocorrelation time and susceptibility uncertainty, the authors show this flow-based approach enables more efficient and ergodic sampling crucial for approaching the continuum limit in lattice gauge theory.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of 'topological freezing' in lattice gauge theory simulations, where standard Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods struggle to explore the full topological space, especially near the continuum limit.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that combining open boundary conditions with Stochastic Normalizing Flows (SNFs) successfully mitigates topological freezing, keeping key diagnostic metrics under control.
method: They employ an out-of-equilibrium trajectory, evolving the system by varying a gauge coupling factor $\lambda_n$ from open to periodic boundary conditions, and using SNFs to facilitate this transition.
model_or_system: The study focuses on pure SU(3) Yang–Mills theory, discretized on a hypercubic lattice. The simulation involves evolving the system's action $S_{\lambda_n}(U^{(n)})$ across the boundary condition change.
key_observables: Topological charge ($Q$), integrated autocorrelation time ($	au_{	ext{int}}$) of $Q^2$, and the statistical uncertainty on the topological susceptibility ($\chi$).
important_parameters: Lattice spacings as fine as 0.03 fm, and the parameter $\lambda_n$ varying from 0 (OBC) to 1 (PBC).
main_assumptions: The approach assumes that SNFs can provide an efficient and ergodic path for sampling the topological sector, combining Non-Equilibrium Monte Carlo (NEMC) concepts with flow-based architectures.
figures_summary: The appendix contains tables comparing topological susceptibility ($\chi$) results from 'Standard' versus 'SNF' algorithms across different cooling steps ($n_{cool}$), and a figure showing histograms of topological charge samples from SNF runs.
paper_structure: The paper develops the methodology using SNFs for out-of-equilibrium sampling, supported by numerical evidence presented in the appendix via tables and figures comparing results against standard methods.
why_interesting: The use of flow-based methods to ensure ergodic sampling in complex, high-dimensional physical systems like lattice gauge theories provides a powerful computational tool applicable to many non-equilibrium quantum many-body problems.
